title: In Situ Microscopy for Real-time Determination of Single-cell Morphology in Bioprocesses
protocol: Identify the cell size range of the microorganism using conventional microscopy.
Define the expected maximum diameter (dmax) of respective cells.
Set dmax to 8 µm for S. cerevisiae.
Choose two measurement gaps of 5x and 10x of the expected dmax of the cells.
Choose the maximum stroboscope intensity.
Choose stroboscope intensities for both gaps with the highest cell concentration so that cells are still visible on images with the lowest light intensity (darkest images).
Choose the minimum stroboscope intensity.
Choose stroboscope intensities for both gaps so that cells are still visible on images with the highest light intensity (brightest images).
Use the lowest cell concentration, which likely appears during the measurement period.
Choose one focus position, which yields the sharpest images for each measurement gap, for both stroboscope intensities and for the concentration range that need to be tested.
Focus cells appropriately so that the image data can be annotated afterwards.
Evaluate the dilution series experiment.
Use the Concentration Calibration (CoCa) Tool to identify the optimal correlation between extracted image features and previously measured concentrations.
Follow the instructions in the software manual for further details.
Identify the optimal correlation between extracted information from image features at various concentrations compared to offline measurements.
Choose the most reasonable measurement gap and stroboscope intensities considering the concentration correlation curve resulting in the smallest weighted root mean square error (WRMSE).
Adjust the measurement gap according to step 1 with a thickness gauge.
Open the graphical user interface Probe Control in the SOPAT dashboard.
Connect the desired probe to the amplifier in the software subsection Actions and press Connect.
Press the Play button to start streaming (Live View).
Clean the measurement gap by spraying ethanol into the gap and carefully wipe any dust or dirt with an optical paper.
Check that the glass of the sensor is free of particles using the Live View in the CamControl.
Place a dry optical paper in the measurement gap.
Open the tab Probe control and adjust the stroboscope intensity to visualize the paper clearly by turning the binding screw until single fibers are seen.
Fill a tube with culture broth.
Dip the microscope into the culture broth so that the gap is fully covered with cell suspension.
Open the tab Probe control and adjust the desired stroboscope intensity according to section 1.
Focus on the cells by fine-tuning the focus binding screw.
Ensure the focus does not change during the experiment.
Define the number of frames per time point to 200 frames per trigger in the menu Triggering.
Set the frame rate to ensure moving particles from a previous frame do not appear in the following frame.
Choose a frame rate that guarantees no repeated particle capture, proven with a test trigger of 200 frames.
Define the directory for saving acquired images in the menu General.
Activate the Start image trigger acquisition button to perform an image acquisition.
Move the tube with culture suspension gently up and down to induce flow through the measuring gap.
Check the acquired images after each measurement for sharpness and repeated particles.
Decrease the frame rate if repeated particles are observed.
Save the settings by selecting C:\Program Files\SOPAT GmbH\monitoringPrograms\camcontrol and pressing Save.
Annotate particles for training the artificial neural network (ANN) using images loaded into "Fiji, ImageJ".
Open the ROI Manager by selecting Analyze | Tools | ROI Manager in the main window of Fiji.
Choose a selection tool such as Wand, freehand, oval, or elliptical selections to draw around the particle.
Refine the selection with the brush tool if necessary.
Add the annotation to the ROI Manager by pressing Add [t].
Mark objects of interest on approximately 15 images: five from the start, five from in between, and five from the end of the experiment.
Decide whether cells need classification into different subclasses based on shape or other features.
Change names accordingly for each selected particle, using one name or abbreviation per class with a counter (e.g., cell_1, cell_2).
Annotate at least 50 particles per class.
Do not annotate objects irrelevant to the process such as gas bubbles or undissolved media components.
Save the annotated objects and the image to a ZIP format.
Send the file to the training network via upload or email.
Use iterative training rounds to improve object recognition accuracy.
Apply the trained workflow (*.wf) with the data batch progressing program Batcher for analyzing test images.
Check object detection on test images through quantification of false positive events.
Quantify particles erroneously detected as cells.
Identify cells that are not correctly classified.
Evaluate cells whose contour has not been well identified.
Quantify false negative events (cells not recognized).
Visualize results in Result Analyzer by starting the program in the dashboard.
Import desired results files with File | Import file or File | Import folders.
Create a chart on the Charts GUI using Chart | Create chart.
Select distribution chart, sensitivity plot, characteristic over time, characteristic over survey points, or feature vs. feature.
Run the workflow in Batcher for all acquired images if results are acceptable.
Combine saved settings from Probe Controller with workflow to create monitoring program.
Use the workflow for future experiments on this culture medium if initial results are satisfactory.
Check annotation on training set and/or continue iterative training rounds if results are not acceptable.
Set the standard deviation (σ) for detected particles.
Adjust the amplitude of the confidence interval based on expected variance.
Set the admitted error (α) between 5% and 10%.
Calculate the number of cells to be identified from each class using equation 1.
Perform a sensitivity analysis at random time points to ensure variability is less than 5%.
Upload saved settings from C:\Program Files\SOPAT GmbH\monitoringPrograms\camcontrol.
Connect the probe to the flow cell or bioreactor.
Perform sterilization for in situ measurements using a pinch flange.
Define the image acquisition rate in the GUI Triggering field as the trigger interval [s].
Adapt the image acquisition rate based on process dynamics, such as lag-phase duration or expected metabolism shifts.
Set an image acquisition sequence of 5 to 10 minutes during batch yeast cultivation for capturing sufficient information about process dynamics.
